reproduction_target: Re-derive the spatial-statistical modeling results reported in Figures 2-6, Table 1 and Supplements 1-8: continuous spatial Gaussian-process (Poisson / ZIP / ZAP) fields for 918 ligand/receptor features over one Day-16 field of view of the Chen et al. 2022 Stereo-seq mouse embryo atlas (CNGB CNP0001543), the ligand-receptor convolution variants, the ELSA spatial-entropy scores, and the latent-space embedding/clustering feature-count sweep.
granularity_note: No workflow file (Snakemake/CWL/Nextflow/WDL/Makefile) is cited in the paper and none is visible on the GitHub landing page, so steps were derived one-per-named-analysis-invocation from Methods sections 2.1.5 and 2.2.1-2.2.6 plus Results 3.1. |S|=10. The repository (github.com/aaron-oz/a-s-omics) contains only two undocumented top-level directories ('Supplements for Publication/code', 'code-spatial-smoothing') and a 3-line README, so no code-derived granularity anchor was available at Stage 1; a Stage-2 read of the repo could plausibly split or merge these steps. NOTE: steps C1 and C3 consume external resources (CNGB accession, FANTOM5 mouse LR database) but env_capture_class is left 'n/a' and the 'fetch-required' subflag is withheld, because A/B/C classification requires the Stage-2 code read.

steps.label: Dataset selection / acquisition: single Day-16 field of view from the Chen et al. 2022 Stereo-seq mouse embryogenesis atlas (CNGB project CNP0001543)

Preprocessing in R: load raw counts, select a visually-recognizable embryonic subregion, filter features to that boundary, collapse ultra-high-resolution data to spatial bins (10, 25, 50); bin-50 used for all figures
Ligand/receptor gene identification: cross-reference the mouse FANTOM5 ligand-receptor database against binned feature names, yielding 974 ligand-or-receptor genes

Feature refinement: retain ligands/receptors with >=2 counts in >=1 cell and non-zero expression in >=0.25% of cells in the field of view, yielding 918 features (1481 downstream ligand-receptor pairs)

Spatial modeling: per-feature Bayesian spatial Gaussian-process model with Poisson observations and Matern covariance, log link, wide Gaussian priors on intercepts and joint penalized-complexity priors on range/variance; fit with R-INLA for all 918 features

Likelihood-model comparison: Poisson vs zero-inflated Poisson vs zero-adjusted Poisson, scored with MAE, RMSE, Dawid-Sebastiani, log score and PIT/residual diagnostics averaged over all observations and 918 features (Table 1, Figure 4)

Raw vs count-normalized input comparison: contrast raw-count topology against count-normalized topology per feature, and test whether jointly modeling nUMI N(s) alters outputs (Figure 3, Supplement 3)

Ligand-receptor convolution variants: product, geometric mean, 'common minimum convolution', and a prototype chemical-kinetics rate-equation approach with a tunable dissociation constant, producing 1481 interaction fields

ELSA (entropy-based local indicator of spatial association) computation over output cluster labels, scanned across the local-distance parameter and averaged across the modeling region to yield a single spatial-entropy score / entrograms (Supplement 6)

Hyperfield dimensionality sweep: rank ligand-receptor features by system-scale variance, then loop over feature counts (10, 50, 100, 150, ..., 1481) performing latent-space embedding, neighborhood-graph construction and clustering with otherwise fixed parameters (scaled, not sum-normalized, no PCA); UMAP/histologic visualization and ELSA per iteration (Figure 6, Supplement 5)

gaps.where: Whole Methods section (2.2.2-2.2.6) and repository README
gaps.missing: 2a - no software versions are stated anywhere. R-INLA is named without a version; R itself is named without a version ('Raw count data were loaded into R'); the ELSA implementation is cited only as literature references (25, 30) with no package name or version. The README is three lines ('A space to share, dump, and collaborate on *omics work') and declares no environment. No renv.lock, Dockerfile, conda environment.yml or sessionInfo appears in the repository root listing. Additionally the latent-space embedding and clustering algorithms of step C10 are never named at all - only 'latent-space embedding', 'neighborhood graph construction' and 'clustering' - which is worse than an unpinned version.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish sessionInfo() or an renv.lock captured from the machine that produced the figures, and name the embedding/clustering packages and functions in Methods 2.2.6.

gaps.where: Methods 2.2.2 - 'we cross-referenced the mouse version of the FANTOM5 database (27) against the feature names of the binned data'
gaps.missing: The FANTOM5 mouse ligand-receptor reference resource is pinned to nothing: no release, no file name, no download URL, no download date, no DOI. Only a literature citation is given. The derived counts (974 ligand-or-receptor genes, 1481 unique pairs) therefore cannot be re-derived deterministically. This is the classic out-of-band/unpinned reference-DB distribution gap; whether it is class B (prose-only pin) or class C (mutable fetch) cannot be decided from prose and requires the Stage-2 code read.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact FANTOM5 file/release and its download date or DOI, or deposit the resolved ligand-receptor pair table alongside the code.

gaps.where: Methods 2.2.1-2.2.2 - 'We selected a single field of view from one of the Day 16 timepoints' and 'a subregion of the embryonic tissue was chosen to be visually recognizable by both experts and non-specialists'
gaps.missing: The specimen-to-analysis mapping is not resolvable. CNGB project CNP0001543 contains a multi-timepoint atlas; neither the sample/section identifier nor which of the Day-16 replicates was used is stated, and the spatial subregion is defined only qualitatively ('visually recognizable') with no bounding coordinates or mask. A re-analyst cannot select the same input tile.
gaps.how_to_close: Give the CNGB sample accession and the bounding-box coordinates or deposit the subregion mask / the bin-50 subregion count matrix as a supplementary file.

gaps.where: Methods 2.2.6 - the feature-count sweep (10, 50, 100, ..., 1481) with latent-space embedding, neighborhood-graph construction and clustering; also the ELSA local-distance scan in 2.1.5
gaps.missing: No random seed is stated anywhere. Latent-space embedding (UMAP is referenced in the Results) and graph-based clustering are stochastic, so the reported cluster counts and per-iteration ELSA values are not bit-reproducible. Under the rubric this caps step C10 at RI with 'distributional-only' matching even if everything else were closed.
gaps.how_to_close: State the seed and show it is consumed by the embedding and clustering calls, or report the results as distributions over repeated runs.

gaps.where: Section 5 Code Availability - 'All code used to create this work is available on GitHub at: https://github.com/aaron-oz/a-s-omics'
gaps.missing: The code is linked but not archivally deposited or pinned. The paper cites a bare repository URL with no commit SHA, no tag and no Zenodo/Software Heritage DOI; the repository has 0 releases and was last pushed 2026-07-27, i.e. after the v2 preprint posting (2025-12-10), so the state that produced the figures is not identifiable. The repository is self-described as 'a space to share, dump, and collaborate', has no README beyond that line, and its two top-level code directories ('Supplements for Publication/code', 'code-spatial-smoothing') carry no documented entry point or mapping from script to figure. This is why the Code axis is scored 1 (reconstructable) rather than 2 (public+exact) on every step.
gaps.how_to_close: Mint a Zenodo DOI or a git tag for the exact analysis state and cite it in the Code Availability statement; add a README mapping scripts to Methods sections and figures.

gaps.where: Methods 2.1.5 / 2.2.5 / 2.2.6 - ELSA, the 'common minimum convolution', and the chemical-kinetics rate-equation convolution
gaps.missing: Key numeric parameters of the custom analyses are absent: the dissociation constant used in the rate-equation convolution is described only as 'a tunable dissociation constant'; the ELSA local-distance values scanned are not enumerated; the Matern smoothness parameter, mesh construction and the concrete hyperparameters of the 'wide' Gaussian priors and of the joint penalized-complexity priors in the R-INLA models are not given. These are custom analysis definitions that live only in the unpinned repository.
gaps.how_to_close: Tabulate the model hyperparameters, the ELSA distance grid and the dissociation constant(s) in a Methods table or a committed config file.
